1	# SMA-869 final whole-branch review

3	Range: `98351cee` (origin/main) .. `eef41525`. Spec and plan as given. I read the
4	full source and docs diff, the full test diff, and the surrounding code in
5	`agent.rs`, `loop_state.rs`, `workflow.rs`, `graph.rs`, `swarm.rs`,
6	`session.rs` (recorder), `runner.rs`, `runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs` and
7	`mcp/src/server.rs`. I did not run tests. I did one pass for the code and one
8	pass for the docs and tests.
9	
10	## Strengths
11	
12	- The eight loop checks sit at the points the spec names, and each one is the
13	  plain "token fired, return" form. No check runs after a terminal event in the
14	  same batch, so the SMA-421/422 rule stays (see "Cross-task check order").
15	- Check 6 (`agent.rs:1548-1552`) uses `!finish_seen`, so goal 12 holds, and the
16	  plan's mutation step pins it.

18	  the recorder sees a resume result and does not treat the run as a rejected
19	  resume (`session.rs:891`). Both paths have a test.
20	- The Graph fix tags each node stream with an end marker and applies the
21	  guard per node. This closes the "sibling starts a successor after a cut
22	  node" gap that the task-4 review found.
23	- The tests fire the run token, use synchronous model streams, and so let the
24	  agent-side check decide, not the `cancelled()` branch of `controlled`.
25	- No `Cargo.toml` version, no `CHANGELOG`, no `Cargo.lock` and no `runtime-*`
26	  `src/` file changed. Every commit type and scope is in `.versionrc`
27	  (`fix`, `test`, `docs`; `core`, `mcp`, `runtime-tokio`, `docs`, `plan`,
28	  `spec`). `.superpowers/` is excluded through `.git/info/exclude`.
29	
30	## Cross-task check order (focus 1)
31	
32	The order in one loop pass is: transition, output guardrail, yield the batch
33	(check 2 at `TurnStarted`), then the `NextAction` arm (checks 3-8).
34	
35	- A batch that holds a terminal event always has `NextAction::Terminate`.
36	  Checks 3, 7 and 8 never see it. Check 2 only matches `TurnStarted`, and no
37	  batch puts `TurnStarted` before a terminal event. So no run that emitted a
38	  terminal event becomes `Cancelled`. The anti-goal holds.
39	- The output guardrail tripwire replaces the batch with `RunFailed`. A cancel
40	  does not change it. Correct: the turn finished.
41	- Structured output: the unconstrained-turn batch is
42	  `[MessageOutput.., TurnStarted(finalizing)]`. A cancel after its `Finish`
43	  yields the complete message, then check 2 stops. The run ends `Cancelled`
44	  and stores one complete assistant message. Correct.
45	- `RepairStarted` has no `TurnStarted`; check 3 covers it.
46	- Max turns and deferral after a tool turn: see Minor 1. A terminal event that
47	  the loop makes *after* the cancel can still win.
48	- Handoff child: the child has the same checks. The parent re-yields and adds
49	  no terminal event (`agent.rs:1768-1776`). `SwarmAgent` adds none either.
50	
51	## Baseline comparison (focus 2)
52	
53	- No cancel: every new check needs `is_cancelled()`. A text turn with no
54	  `Finish` and no cancel still completes (guard test). A workflow child with no
55	  terminal event and no cancel keeps the old behaviour (guard test).
56	- Tests in other crates: I grepped every `crates/*/tests` and `crates/*/src`
57	  file that calls `.cancel()`. The only test that pinned "a pre-fired token
58	  completes" was `run_control.rs::prefired_cancel_still_completes_ready_run`,
59	  which the branch replaced. `core/tests/tool_calls_not_run.rs` already
60	  expects no terminal event. The `evals/tests/mock.rs` tests are model-level.
61	  runtime-axum, runtime-actix and runtime-agentcore have cancel code only in
62	  `src/` and get the fix through the existing "no terminal + token fired" rule.
63	  runtime-agentcore MCP mode reuses `McpAgentServer`, so it gets the MCP fix.
64	  runtime-temporal does not run this loop.
65	- Behaviour change that the spec does not name: `OnRunComplete` no longer
66	  fires for a run that ended `Completed` with cut text before. See Minor 5.
67	
68	## Issues
69	
70	### Critical
71	
72	None.
73	
74	### Important
75	
76	1. **The book now promises more than the code does.**
77	   - `docs/book/src/concepts/agent-loop.md:149`: "Otherwise, through a runner,
78	     a fired token ends the run as `RunError::Cancelled`. This is true also
79	     when the token fired before the run started."
80	   - `docs/book/src/concepts/observability-evaluation.md:348`: "A cancel ends
81	     the run."
82	   - Why it is wrong: there are reachable paths where the token fired first
83	     and the run still ends with a real terminal event that the loop makes
84	     later. (a) A pre-fired token with an input guardrail tripwire or an
85	     `OnRunStart` deny ends `RunFailed` (the spec accepted that these run).
86	     (b) A cancel during the tools of the last allowed turn ends
87	     `RunFailed(MaxTurnsExceeded)` (`loop_state.rs:516-525`). (c) A cancel in a
88	     tool batch where another call defers ends `RunDeferred`
89	     (`loop_state.rs:456-497`). (d) A cancel after `Finish` of the final text
90	     turn ends `Completed` (goal 12, by design). The `Runner::run` rustdoc
91	     (`runner.rs:109-116`) still says "a caller cannot assume cancel ⇒
92	     Cancelled". The book now says the opposite, so the two contradict.
93	   - Also `agent-loop.md:69` reads as the full list of no-terminal exits, but
94	     it omits a model error after the cancel (checks 4 and 5).
95	   - Fix (docs only):
96	     - `agent-loop.md:149`: "A terminal event wins over a cancel. If the run
97	       ends with no terminal event and the token fired, a runner reports
98	       `RunError::Cancelled`. The loop ends with no terminal event at each
99	       point where it checks the token (see the list under 'Terminal'). This
100	       also applies when the token fired before the run started. Some steps
101	       still run before the first check: the `OnRunStart` hook and the input
102	       guardrails. A step that ends the run with a terminal event, such as a
103	       guardrail tripwire or the max-turns limit, still wins. Timeout stays
104	       best-effort."
105	     - `agent-loop.md:69`: add "or when the model call or its stream returned
106	       an error after the token fired".
107	     - `observability-evaluation.md:348`: "A cancel before a terminal event
108	       ends the run."
109	   - If you prefer to close (b) and (c) in code instead, see Minor 1, and then
110	     keep only (a) and (d) in the text.
111	
112	### Minor
113	
114	1. **A cancel during the tools of the last allowed turn, or next to a deferred
115	   call, does not end `Cancelled`.** `agent.rs:1608-1665` runs the tools, then
116	   the `ToolResults` / `ToolResultsWithDeferrals` transition emits
117	   `RunFailed(MaxTurnsExceeded)` or `RunDeferred`. No check runs between them.
118	   Goal 3 says "a cancel while a tool runs ends the run as `Cancelled`".
119	   Baseline gives the same result, so this is not a regression. Fix options:
120	   (a) document it (Important 1); or (b) in the `for ev in events` loop, when
121	   `loop_state` is `ExecutingTools` and the token fired, return at the first
122	   terminal event of the batch, after the `ToolOutputItem` events. Do (b) only
123	   for `RunFailed(MaxTurns)`. Keep `RunDeferred`, because the deferral slot
124	   was already recorded (`agent.rs:1660`) and the session must store it.
125	2. **Check 3 has no test that fails without it.** On every tested path, check 2
126	   (`TurnStarted`) stops the run first. Check 3 alone decides only when an
127	   `OnTurnStart` hook or the turn checkpoint fires the token, or on the
128	   `RepairStarted` path. Goal 2 also says `OnTurnStart` must not run, and no
129	   test counts it. Fix: add to `cancel_boundaries.rs` a test with a hook that
130	   calls `ctx.cancel().cancel()` on `HookEvent::OnTurnStart { turn: 0 }`.
131	   Assert `Err(RunError::Cancelled)` and `model.calls() == 0`. Mutation-check
132	   it by removing check 3.
133	3. **A misleading test comment.**
134	   `runtime-tokio/tests/cancel_boundaries.rs` (`cancel_while_a_tool_runs_is_cancelled`)
135	   says "Guard: check 3 ... already covers this case". The test fails on
136	   `main`, so by the spec's rule it is not a guard. Also check 2, not check 3,
137	   stops the run, because the tool-results batch holds `TurnStarted`. Fix:
138	   "Check 2 (at `TurnStarted`) stops this run before the second model call."
139	4. **The MCP change is not in the book or the rustdoc.** A cancelled run now
140	   gives the error result `agent run was cancelled`. Neither
141	   `docs/book/src/concepts/mcp-integration.md:86` nor the `McpAgentServer`
142	   rustdoc (`mcp/src/server.rs:29-33`) says so. The CLAUDE.md book rule asks
143	   for this in the same PR. Fix: add one sentence to each: "A cancelled run
144	   that ends with no terminal event returns an MCP error result
145	   (`agent run was cancelled`)."
146	5. **`OnRunComplete` no longer fires for a cancelled run that completed
147	   before.** Before, a cut text turn emitted `RunCompleted`, so the
148	   `Terminate` arm fired `OnRunComplete`. Now every cancel exit returns before
149	   that arm. This matches the existing cancel exit in the `acc.finish()` error
150	   branch, so it is consistent. A host that used `OnRunComplete` for cleanup
151	   can see a difference. Fix: in
152	   `docs/book/src/concepts/permissions-guardrails-hooks.md:255`, add
153	   "`OnRunComplete` does not fire for a run that ends with no terminal event
154	   (a cancel)."
155	6. **The second graph test depends on the poll order of `SelectAll`.**
156	   `core/tests/graph.rs` (`cancelled_root_stops_graph_before_sibling_successor_starts`)
157	   passes only because `SelectAll` polls `cut` before `done`, so the end
158	   marker of `cut` comes before the `RunCompleted` of `done`. With the other
159	   order, `succ` starts and the test fails. The order is stable for the pinned
160	   `futures-util`, so the test is not flaky today. Fix: add a comment that
161	   states this, so a `futures-util` bump that breaks it is easy to diagnose.
162	7. **The Parallel test cannot tell "any branch" from "all branches".**
163	   `core/tests/workflow_parallel.rs` (`cancelled_branch_ends_parallel_with_no_terminal`)
164	   uses two branches with no terminal event. Fix (optional): make one branch
165	   emit `RunCompleted`.
166	
167	## Ledger Minors triage
168	
169	| Ledger item | Ruling | Reason |
170	|---|---|---|
171	| T1: test boilerplate in `cancel_boundaries.rs` | Leave | Style only. |
172	| T1: `cancel_after_finish_still_completes` depends on no `Pending` before `RunCompleted` | **Fix before merge** | One comment line. Same class as T4 FIFO; a later async hook would make the failure look like a check-6 regression. |
173	| T1: duplicated `"run cancelled"` literal | Leave | Copies the existing `run_streamed.rs:140` pattern. |
174	| T2: `cancel_between_turns_makes_no_second_model_call` has no "Guard:" comment | Leave | The test fails on `main`, so it is not a guard. Fix Minor 3 instead (the comment on the other test is the wrong one). |
175	| T3: repeated `close_open_transfers` + `not_run` sequence | Leave | A helper inside `stream!` is awkward; three sites. |
176	| T3: handoff-resume test does not assert the `RunFailed("run cancelled")` terminal | Leave | It asserts the important facts (no `AgentUpdated`, zero calls, no open deferral). |
177	| T4: graph test depends on `SelectAll` FIFO order | **Fix before merge** | Comment only (Minor 6). |
178	| T4: `OnSubagentStop` not fired for the cut graph node | Leave | Graph fired it only on a child terminal event before the change too. |
179	| T5: no MCP regression test for "cancel after a terminal keeps success" | Leave | The condition is one line and is clear by reading. Cheap to add if a change wave happens anyway. |
180	| T5: cosmetic early `return` in `server.rs` | Leave | Style only. |
181	| T6: `agent-loop.md` trigger list omits the turn boundary and the model error | **Fix before merge** | Part of Important 1. |
182	| T6: streamed `RunFailed` and workflow / `AgentAsTool` / MCP pass-through not documented | Leave, except MCP | The MCP part is Minor 4. The rest is a future book improvement. |
183	| T6: "A cancel ends the run." too strong | **Fix before merge** | Part of Important 1. |
184	| T6: awkward sentence "This is true also when ..." | **Fix before merge** | The Important 1 rewrite replaces it. |
185	
186	## Declined to judge
187	
188	- Spans: a cancelled exit leaves `agent.run` and `gen_ai.chat` with no status
189	  and no usage. The spec rejected a trace mark, so I did not grade it.
190	- `collect` with no runner still returns `Ok` for a cancelled run. This is a
191	  spec non-goal.
192	- The `OnRunStart` hook and input guardrails run on a pre-fired token. The spec
193	  accepted this. I only flag the docs (Important 1).
194	- Live stream clients still see `TokenDelta` text of a cut turn. Spec non-goal.
195	- A tool result that the recorder stores, followed by no assistant turn, after
196	  a cancel at `TurnStarted`. The recorder already makes the log
197	  provider-valid; the session shape is the same as the existing mid-tool
198	  cancel case.
199	- The release effect: commit `4e1c6bcb` (`fix(core)`) also touches
200	  runtime-tokio tests, and the evals README edit touches a packaged file, so
201	  release-plz gives runtime-tokio and evals patch bumps too. This is harmless
202	  and the expected repo behaviour, so I did not grade it.
203	
204	## Assessment
205	
206	**Ready to merge:** With fixes.
207	
208	**Reasoning:** The code is correct for the spec's goals and keeps the
209	"terminal wins" anti-goal on every path that I traced. The one Important
210	finding is in the docs: the book now gives a stronger guarantee than the code
211	and contradicts the `Runner::run` rustdoc. The rest are small test and doc
212	gaps.

   test counts it. Fix: add to `cancel_boundaries.rs` a test with a hook that
   calls `ctx.cancel().cancel()` on `HookEvent::OnTurnStart { turn: 0 }`.
   Assert `Err(RunError::Cancelled)` and `model.calls() == 0`. Mutation-check
   it by removing check 3.
3. **A misleading test comment.**
   `runtime-tokio/tests/cancel_boundaries.rs` (`cancel_while_a_tool_runs_is_cancelled`)
   says "Guard: check 3 ... already covers this case". The test fails on
   `main`, so by the spec's rule it is not a guard. Also check 2, not check 3,
   stops the run, because the tool-results batch holds `TurnStarted`. Fix:
   "Check 2 (at `TurnStarted`) stops this run before the second model call."
4. **The MCP change is not in the book or the rustdoc.** A cancelled run now
   gives the error result `agent run was cancelled`. Neither
   `docs/book/src/concepts/mcp-integration.md:86` nor the `McpAgentServer`
   rustdoc (`mcp/src/server.rs:29-33`) says so. The CLAUDE.md book rule asks
   for this in the same PR. Fix: add one sentence to each: "A cancelled run
   that ends with no terminal event returns an MCP error result
   (`agent run was cancelled`)."
5. **`OnRunComplete` no longer fires for a cancelled run that completed
   before.** Before, a cut text turn emitted `RunCompleted`, so the
   `Terminate` arm fired `OnRunComplete`. Now every cancel exit returns before
   that arm. This matches the existing cancel exit in the `acc.finish()` error
   branch, so it is consistent. A host that used `OnRunComplete` for cleanup
   can see a difference. Fix: in
   `docs/book/src/concepts/permissions-guardrails-hooks.md:255`, add
   "`OnRunComplete` does not fire for a run that ends with no terminal event
   (a cancel)."
6. **The second graph test depends on the poll order of `SelectAll`.**
   `core/tests/graph.rs` (`cancelled_root_stops_graph_before_sibling_successor_starts`)
   passes only because `SelectAll` polls `cut` before `done`, so the end
   marker of `cut` comes before the `RunCompleted` of `done`. With the other
   order, `succ` starts and the test fails. The order is stable for the pinned
   `futures-util`, so the test is not flaky today. Fix: add a comment that
   states this, so a `futures-util` bump that breaks it is easy to diagnose.
7. **The Parallel test cannot tell "any branch" from "all branches".**
   `core/tests/workflow_parallel.rs` (`cancelled_branch_ends_parallel_with_no_terminal`)
   uses two branches with no terminal event. Fix (optional): make one branch
   emit `RunCompleted`.

| T3: repeated `close_open_transfers` + `not_run` sequence | Leave | A helper inside `stream!` is awkward; three sites. |
| T3: handoff-resume test does not assert the `RunFailed("run cancelled")` terminal | Leave | It asserts the important facts (no `AgentUpdated`, zero calls, no open deferral). |

  and no usage. The spec rejected a trace mark, so I did not grade it.
- `collect` with no runner still returns `Ok` for a cancelled run. This is a
  spec non-goal.
